name: Polish Bank
description: Polish Bank (also simply known as 'Bank' or the 'Russian' variation) is an intense, high-stakes comparing game purely designed for gambling. It belongs to the same family of games as 'Red Dog' and 'Slippery Sam'. Players bet against a central pool that they hold a higher card of a specific suit than a revealed target. It is known for its strict 'Blind Betting' rules, where touching your cards before wagering is a penalized offense.

content.text: Polish Bank (also simply known as 'Bank' or the 'Russian' variation) is an intense, high-stakes comparing game purely designed for gambling. It belongs to the same family of games as 'Red Dog' and 'Slippery Sam'. Players bet against a central pool that they hold a higher card of a specific suit than a revealed target. It is known for its strict 'Blind Betting' rules, where touching your cards before wagering is a penalized offense.
Likely developed from 18th-century European banking games like 'Pharaon' and 'Basset'. It became widely popular in Eastern Europe and among immigrant communities in the US.
Four to seven players; five or six is ideal for pace and pool size (Bank requires a banker plus punters).
Standard 52-card deck of French playing cards; ace is high and two is low. One pack per round.
